attackPatternTags.quote: When unable to reach the player, he may teleport to their location.
King Slime attempts to deal contact damage to the player by hopping towards them, and additionally summons slimes to aid him in the fight.
If the player dies or gets more than 187.5 tiles away from King Slime, he will teleport to the bottom-right corner of the world and despawn in 0.17 seconds.
Most bosses and event bosses can pass through blocks of all types, with the exception of King Slime, Queen Slime, Flying Dutchman, and Deerclops (most of the time).

strategies.quote: The pattern of his jumps is predictable and repeatedly: two normal, one small, and one high.
After the high jump, the King Slime can teleport to the player.
When King Slime is about to teleport, he shrinks, and his map icon will get closer to the ground.
Getting too far away from King Slime will make it teleport to the player, meaning that the player cannot escape by simply running offscreen.
King Slime becomes smaller and faster the lower his health is, which makes him harder to hit.
Piercing weapons can not only damage King Slime, but also kill the additional slimes he spawns.
If he or his slimes reach the platform, drop down temporarily and use hooks or double-jumps to return; this will cause King Slime and his minions to drop down as well, following you.
King Slime is very slow in liquids.
However, when damaged it will spawn Spiked Slimes in addition to regular Blue Slimes.

strategies.quote: After spawning 3 or 4 Servants, the Eye will charge at you, attempting to ram you 3 times before hovering once more, so be prepared to evade.
It can be helpful to begin to evade after the 3rd servant is spawned, as this will often allow you to dodge its first charge.
The Servants are weak and can be killed for Hearts, or, if there is enough room, the player can simply keep moving in one direction to avoid them.
Make sure to take advantage of its transformation sequence as much as possible, since it just spins in place for a few moments and you can still damage it.
For the last half of the fight, the boss sheds its iris to reveal a fanged mouth. It moves slightly faster and deals more damage when it hits you, but it also has no defense.
With a wide enough arena, running in a straight line while the Eye of Cthulhu does his quick charge is fast enough to avoid any damage, and allows the player to attack continuously.
The boss looks at the player it will follow, which can be helpful information in multiplayer.
In the first phase of the fight it spawns more servants and enters the second phase at 65% health instead of 50%, spawning 4–5 more Servants in that process.

summon.quote: The Eater of Worlds spawns upon destroying every third Shadow Orb in a Corruption world. It can also be summoned manually by using a Worm Food in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.

time.quote: in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time

attackPatternTags.quote: While burrowing, it gradually builds up speed in the direction of the player, up to a limit.
If the player dies or is in neither the Corruption nor the Crimson, all of the worms begin fleeing by moving downwards.

prepChecklist.quote: If it goes too high and the Corruption background disappears, the Eater of Worlds will start despawning.

prepChecklist.quote: A room with a Bed next to your arena can let you teleport there easily, but be careful that the path from the Orb to arena does not go through any non-Corrupted areas (lest the boss despawn).

prepChecklist.quote: To not get interrupted by the Eaters of Souls, it's recommended to place an Eater of Souls Banner to minimize their damage.

prepChecklist.quote: Ironskin and Regeneration Potions can really help mitigate any hits you take.

prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: Beware that, when a segment dies, the segments in front and behind will detach and separately attack the player.
To avoid getting overwhelmed by many worms at once, it may be helpful to only aim for the head or tail of the worm, as these segments will not cause the boss to split further when killed.
If you destroy a middle segment, concentrate on the smaller worm, since the larger one can be easy to predict and dodge.

Like other worm enemies, once the Eater's head passes a given point, every body segment must follow. This allows the player to stand next to the body, attacking every segment as it goes by. The player should be wary of the head looping back around.
In Classic Mode, Grenades are an effective weapon against the Eater. That is not true in higher difficulties, since the Eater gains resistance to explosives.
The Eater of Worlds will start to flee underground if the player leaves the Corruption biome, but will not immediately despawn.
Vile Spit is the Eater of Worlds' most dangerous attack, so it is important to bring sufficient mobility accessories and make an arena that enables you to dodge.

strategies.quote: Brain of Cthulhu has 2 phases, with the latter starting after all Creepers have been dealt with.
Jump out of the way, either by using your platforms or with an extra jump, then attack the Creepers. Use piercing weapons to speed up the process.
Creepers have low individual health and are especially susceptible to the On Fire! and Frostburn debuffs.

When all of the Creepers are dead, the Brain will split, revealing a Heart with an Eye on the inside. The Brain teleports much more frequently, often at unexpected angles, and will try to ram into you.
If you have a weapon with high knockback, it will excel at dealing with the Brain, so much so that it's possible to stand in one location and attack it whenever it gets close.
During the second phase, the Brain will spawn clones of itself around the player.

strategies.quote: When she charges you, use platforms and/or a double jump or better to dodge upwards.
When she summons her Bees, use a weapon that can pierce targets and aim for her tail to stop the Bees the moment they spawn.
If any Bees manage to escape then use a sword with a large swing to clear them out.
If she's using the stinger-shooting phase, keep moving back and forth.
Getting hit by a stinger inflicts a Poisoned debuff that will last longer than running into Queen Bee, so make sure to dodge it.
Solid blocks can help to block the stingers.
Queen Bee is one of the few bosses that does not despawn when the player teleports away.
As the Queen Bee's health goes down, she will become a lot more aggressive, shooting more stingers and having much faster charges.

strategies.quote: Attacking the hands first is advised, as destroying them both will make it very easy to dodge Skeletron for the rest of the battle. This is pretty much mandatory in Expert Mode, as Skeletron gains 25 defense for each hand it has alive.
Timing is key in order to defend from the hands: after dodging them, use piercing weapons to deal damage to both arms (and Skeletron's skull, if it happens to align with them).
Try to avoid staying above or far to one side of Skeletron for a long time.

After some time, Skeletron will use its spinning attack. Skeletron moves slowly, but they constantly follow the player. During this attack, Skeletron's defense is lowered to zero, but gains more attack. The player should use the fastest weapon at their disposal to deal a lot of damage. However, make sure to constantly move; if the player gets hit by it, they might get stunlocked and take a lot of damage.
Skulls are blocked by solid blocks, so a barrier between the player and Skeletron can let the player attack Skeletron using a yoyo with impunity.
In Expert Mode, if the player keeps moving in different directions, most of the homing skulls will miss.

strategies.quote: Avoid lingering directly above Deerclops, as the Shadow Hands it summons in this situation are very dangerous.
The player can run between Deerclops's legs without taking damage. This is useful for avoiding the first two Ice Spike attacks, but the player should not stick around for the third.

If it is close to the player, Deerclops will smash the ground, summoning a wave of Ice Spikes that quickly travels towards the player. Every third consecutive wave does not go as far, instead spreading in both directions.

If the player is more than 30 tiles away, Deerclops will turn a dark shade of purple, two reddish, semi-transparent images of Deerclops will begin spinning around it, and it becomes immune to all damage.
Due to being able to inflict Slow from a large range, accessories like the Anklet of the Wind or Magiluminescence alongside Swiftness Potions can help make the fight much more manageable.
The Frozen debuff from the Ice Spike attack is capable of interrupting a player's extending grappling hook, causing them to drop to the ground.
Shadow Hands are summoned more frequently as Deerclops's life gets lower. Shadow Hands predict the player's movements.

strategies.quote: When avoiding The Destroyer, go up, not down.
Getting stuck under The Destroyer is extremely dangerous, so be sure to have an arena with platforms or good jump items.
Probes should be taken out as soon as possible, since they interfere with the fight and additionally serve as a steady source of Hearts.
Find a balance between damaging the worm and dealing with Probes to survive the fight.
For extra risk and reward, line up with the head (which has no defense) and fire down the length of its body.
Using the minimap to see where The Destroyer will surface can greatly help with dodging.
It is very important not to get touched by the head, as it can deal massive damage, bringing players from full health to zero in only two hits.

summon.quote: Duke Fishron is summoned by fishing in the Ocean at any time, using a Truffle Worm as bait

time.quote: summoned by fishing in the Ocean at any time

attackPatternTags.quote: Duke Fishron lunges at the player exactly five times, traveling through blocks
he remains stationary for a second and transforms
Straying too far from the surface Ocean area during the fight causes Duke Fishron to "enrage"
before exploding and dealing damage while inflicting the Wet debuff for 3–8 seconds
Duke Fishron will despawn if all players are dead or if the targeted player is more than 350 tiles away from him.

prepChecklist.text: Build the arena over the Ocean: away from it he enrages
prepChecklist.quote: The arena must be located in the Ocean, unless you're very confident that you can beat an enraged Fishron, which is usually not recommended.

prepChecklist.text: Stack 3–5 rows of platforms about 50 tiles apart: the tornadoes are tall
prepChecklist.quote: Make an arena with 3 - 5 rows of Platforms, each about 50 tiles apart due to the height of the Cthulhunados.

prepChecklist.text: Find a Truffle Worm in the underground Glowing Mushroom biome
prepChecklist.quote: Truffle Worms can be found underground in the Glowing Mushroom biome during Hardmode.

prepChecklist.text: Drink an Inferno Potion to destroy his Detonating Bubbles
prepChecklist.quote: Inferno Potion is highly recommended as it will destroy the Detonating Bubbles that Duke Fishron spawns before they reach the player.

prepChecklist.text: Bring fast wings: quick aerial movement is a must
prepChecklist.quote: Quick aerial movement is a must-have for the fight.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Regeneration, Ironskin, Endurance and Lifeforce Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Regeneration Potion and Ironskin Potion, Endurance and Lifeforce will improve survivability.

prepChecklist.text: No platform over the water? Drink Water Walking Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Water Walking Potions can be used as a substitute for a platform in the Ocean.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: Duke Fishron's charges aim for where the player is, not where they will be. Because of this, moving perpendicularly with his charges will cause him to completely miss.
Also, note that Duke Fishron's first attack will always be bubbles.
Do not fly all the way into the space layer, or the reduced gravity will render you helpless.
Once the bubble strikes the player, they should do all they can to quickly move, to prevent the Cthulhunado from spawning on top of them.
Contact with a Cthulhunado, either immediately after its spawning or later, should be avoided by all possible means, as they deal 100 contact damage.
Though his difficulty makes him a post-Plantera or Golem boss, it is possible to defeat him before the mechanical bosses.
When Duke Fishron drops below 15% health, he will transform again and the background will notably darken, while making himself invisible except for his glowing eyes.

strategies.quote: As there won't be many opportunities to deal damage, you should try to deal as much burst damage as possible during his charges.

strategies.quote: In Expert Mode, the Shield of Cthulhu can be used to great effect, providing brief invincibility frames when dashing into him.

strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Melee users:" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Bananarang and Chain Guillotines are the best options against this boss before any mechanical bosses with the former being better in the second phase and the latter being better at fighting him at a close range.

summon.quote: The Lunatic Cultist is summoned after killing the Cultists that spawn at the Dungeon's entrance after Skeletron and Golem have been defeated.

attackPatternTags.quote: Between each attack, the Lunatic Cultist teleports to a position above the player's current location.
Fires a burst of three / four homing, high-velocity Fireballs
Performs a ritual to summon extra enemies.
that explode upon contact with the player or solid blocks, inflicting the On Fire! debuff
if one is too far away from it (e.g. by using a Magic Mirror or Recall Potion), it will despawn

prepChecklist.text: Build a basic arena with a few rows of platforms near the Dungeon (a Skeletron arena works)
prepChecklist.quote: A basic arena with some rows of platforms will suffice. If the player made an arena for Skeletron, they can reuse it here.

prepChecklist.text: Be ready for the Lunar Events: defeating it starts them at once
prepChecklist.quote: Beating the Lunatic Cultist causes the Lunar Events to begin immediately, and there is no way to de-summon them thereafter (aside from defeating all of the Celestial Pillars).

prepChecklist.text: Fight at night: the decoy cultists glow
prepChecklist.quote: It is recommended to fight the Cultist at night, as the fake cultists will glow.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Hunter Potion to spot the real Cultist among its clones
prepChecklist.quote: Hunter Potion will show the real cultist when cloning itself.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Regeneration, Endurance, Lifeforce and Ironskin Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, Lifeforce Potion, and Ironskin Potion will greatly increase survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Swiftness Potion for mobility
prepChecklist.quote: Swiftness Potion will increase mobility.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a Frozen Shield for knockback immunity and less damage taken
prepChecklist.quote: The Frozen Shield is a powerful accessory that grants immunity to knockback, and reduces damage taken.

prepChecklist.text: Afterwards, keep a Magic Mirror or Recall Potion ready in case a Celestial Pillar spawns nearby
prepChecklist.quote: it is recommended to immediately pick up the Lunatic Cultist's drops and teleport back to a safe base using a Magic Mirror or Recall Potion to prevent from being unexpectedly ambushed by dangerous enemies spawned from the Lunar Events.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: If the real Lunatic Cultist is damaged, neither of these two powerful minions will spawn in.
When the ritual starts, the real Cultist is the copy that is furthest away from the player.
When hovered over, decoys will always display as having 10000/10000 health, while the real Cultist will display its true health value instead.
Using Autopause grants as much time as needed for identifying the real Cultist.
Many of the Lunatic Cultist's attacks can be blocked by hiding behind solid blocks, including its lightning bolts and fireballs.
By remain very close to the boss and slowly circling him using a flying mount, the attacks are closer together and easier to dodge.
In Expert Mode, when the health of the boss is below 50%, the Cultist may also spawn Ancient Dooms that fire purple projectiles in a cross shape.

entries.name: Moon Lord
entries.statsUnknown: Multi-part boss (head, two hands and core, each with its own health and defense); no boss-level row.

summon.quote: The Moon Lord will spawn after destroying the four Celestial Pillars or can be summoned manually using a Celestial Sigil in any world where Golem has been defeated.

attackPatternTags.quote: The Moon Lord will teleport to the nearest player in a large flash of white light
When destroyed, each eye then spawns an invulnerable True Eye of Cthulhu.
The Moon Lord's hands shoot two projectiles at once which home onto the player
Moon Leech inflicts the Moon Bite debuff to the associated player

prepChecklist.text: Build a long sky bridge on both sides of your spawn point (700–1000 platforms)
prepChecklist.quote: Ideally, it should extend quite far from either side of your spawn point (700-1000 platform blocks should suffice).

prepChecklist.text: Build a house for the Nurse nearby
prepChecklist.quote: although it is still wise to build a nearby house for the Nurse

prepChecklist.text: Craft Super Healing Potions from Celestial Fragments
prepChecklist.quote: Super Healing Potions are absolutely worth the Celestial Fragments required to craft them.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Regeneration, Endurance, Lifeforce and Ironskin Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Regeneration Potion, Endurance Potion, Lifeforce Potion, and to a lesser extent, Ironskin Potion will greatly increase survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Rage, Summoning and Wrath Potions for damage
prepChecklist.quote: Rage Potion, Summoning Potion, and Wrath Potion will improve DPS.

prepChecklist.text: Equip your best wings, unless you fly on a mount
prepChecklist.quote: Wings are almost a requirement when dodging the Moon Lord's attacks, unless the player is using a flying mount.

prepChecklist.text: Bring a Rod of Discord to teleport out of the Phantasmal Deathray
prepChecklist.quote: It can also be dodged with a Rod of Discord by teleporting out of its path.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a Frozen Shield for knockback immunity
prepChecklist.quote: The Frozen Shield provides crucial knockback immunity that will allow you to avoid being thrown around by enemy attacks.

strategies.quote: Keeping a distance while dodging the Moon Lord's attacks is crucial. In particular, his Phantasmal Deathray should be avoided at all costs.
It is advisable to kill the eye on the head first.
Because of this attack it is a bad idea to keep the Moon Lord offscreen, as the player won't be able to see it coming.
The eyes will look at the player when preparing the attack, so you can predict it as well.
Running away in this case is better, as the True Eyes' Deathrays have much shorter reach compared to the Moon Lord's.
Using homing weapons or ammo like Chlorophyte Bullets allow the player to focus on dodging.
However, since the Moon Lord's eyes remove all debuffs when they close, the player will have to reapply them accordingly.
There are no important changes in these modes outside of increased damage.
